key: ["Around 2600 BCE, on the Indus and the Ghaggar-Hakra, towns become cities. Baked-brick houses line planned streets over covered drains, and their traders reach from Afghanistan to the Gulf. After 1900 BCE the great cities empty. Then comes a different voice, the hymns of the Rigveda, the oldest Indian words that can still be read. Iron spreads across the Ganga plain, and by the fifth century BCE sixteen great realms contest the north.", "sarvam:varun_en_suspense@en-IN", "+6%", "+0Hz", null, 1.0, 0.0, "v3"]
